segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Hello, Pembroke Cycling Holidays, Bob speaking.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Oh hello. I’ve seen your advert for people to lead cycle trips. Are you the right person to speak to?

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Yes, I am. Could I have your name, please?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: It’s Margaret Smith.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Are you looking for a permanent job, Margaret?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: No, temporary. I’ve got a permanent job starting in a few months’ time, and I want to do something else until then.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: What work do you do?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: This will probably sound crazy – I used to be a lawyer, and then I made a complete career change and I’m going to be a doctor. I’ve just finished my training.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Right. And have you had any experience of leading cycle trips?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Yes, I’ve led several bike tours in Africa. The trip to India that I had arranged to lead next month has now been cancelled, so when I saw you were advertising for tour leaders, I decided to apply.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: OK. Now we normally have two or three leaders on a trip, depending on the size of the group. Some tours are for very experienced cyclists, but we’ve got a tour coming up soon in Spain, which is proving so popular we need an additional leader. It’s a cycling holiday for families. Would that suit you?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: It certainly would. I enjoy working with children, and I probable need some more experience before I go on a really challenging trip.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: That tour includes several teenagers: have you worked with that age group before?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Yes, I’m a volunteer worker in a youth club, where I help people to improve their cycling skills. Before that I helped out in a cycling club where I taught beginners.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Well that’s great. Now the trip I mentioned is just for a fortnight, but there might be the possibility of leading other tours after that. Would that fit in with your plans?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: That’s be fine. I’ll be free for five months. My job is due to start on October the 2nd, and I’m available from May the 1st until late September.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Good. Now is there anything I need to know about the food you eat? We usually have one or two people in the group who don’t eat meat, or have some sort of food allergy, so we’re always very careful about that.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Yes, I’m allergic to cheese. Would that be a problem?

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: No, as long as we have enough notice, we can deal with that.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: That’s great. ——————–

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: It sounds really interesting – would you like me to fill in an application form?

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Yes, please. Where should I post it to?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Could you send it to 27 Arbuthnot Place – A-R-B-U-T-H-N-O-T – Place, Dumfries.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: And what’s the postcode, please?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: DG7 4PH.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Was that P Papa or B Bravo?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: P Papa.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Got that. If you could return the application form by Friday this week, we can interview you on Tuesday next week. Say half past two. Would that be possible for you?

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Yes, it’s fine. You’re quite a long way from where I live, so I’ll drive over on Monday. Should I bring anything to the interview?

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: We’ll have your application form, of course, but we’ll need to see any certificates you’ve got that are relevant, in cycling, first aid, or whatever.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: And at the interview we’d like to find out about your experience of being a tour guide, so could you prepare a ten-minute talk about that, please? You don’t need slides or any complicated equipment – just some notes.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Right. I’ll start thinking about that straightaway!

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Good. Well, we’ll look forward to receiving your application form, and we’ll contact you to confirm the interview.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Thanks very much.

segments.speaker: BOB
segments.en: Thank you, Margaret. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: MARGARET
segments.en: Bye.
